content.text: The Full List With Context

When it comes to building a sovereign commerce infrastructure, there are several key components to consider. First, you need a reliable hosting solution that can handle traffic and scale as needed. Then, you need a backend logic system that can process payments and handle orders. You also need a secure way to store and deliver digital products. Finally, you need a payment processing system that can handle multiple cryptocurrencies and doesn't require KYC or buyer accounts. By combining these components, you can create a fully functional online store that operates independently of traditional payment platforms.
Why Each Item on This List Matters

Each component of a sovereign commerce infrastructure plays a critical role in ensuring the smooth operation of your online store. Without a reliable hosting solution, your store may be slow or unresponsive, driving away customers. Without a secure backend logic system, you may be vulnerable to hacking or data breaches. And without a reliable payment processing system, you may struggle to receive payments from customers. By prioritizing each of these components, you can build a robust and reliable infrastructure that supports your business goals.
The Ones Most Creators Get Wrong

Many digital creators make the mistake of relying on third-party platforms or workarounds to process payments. This can lead to a lack of control over your business, as well as increased fees and reduced profitability. Others may try to build their own infrastructure from scratch, which can be time-consuming and require significant technical expertise. By understanding the common pitfalls and mistakes, you can avoid them and build a more effective and efficient sovereign commerce infrastructure.
Build a sovereign commerce infrastructure today.
How to Prioritise What to Implement First

When building a sovereign commerce infrastructure, it's essential to prioritize the most critical components first. Start by setting up a reliable hosting solution and backend logic system, then focus on implementing a secure payment processing system. From there, you can add additional features and components as needed. By prioritizing the most essential elements, you can ensure that your infrastructure is robust and reliable, and that you can start selling digital products quickly and efficiently.
Putting the List Into a Deployable Stack

By combining the key components of a sovereign commerce infrastructure, you can create a fully functional online store that operates independently of traditional payment platforms. This can be achieved by using a combination of free and paid tools, such as GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and NOWPayments. By leveraging these tools, you can build a deployable stack that supports your business goals and allows you to sell digital products with confidence and control.
How can creators in Africa sell digital products to international buyers?

Global access through sovereign infrastructure works because every layer of the stack is geography-neutral by design. Cloudflare Pages serves your storefront from data centers close to your buyer — whether they are in London or Lagos, the page loads in under 200 milliseconds. NOWPayments generates a unique payment address for each transaction — the buyer sends crypto from any wallet, anywhere in the world. The blockchain confirms the transaction regardless of which country the sender is in. Your Cloudflare Worker receives the webhook and processes the order using the same logic for every buyer.
Take control of your digital business.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Global access to digital product revenue is not contingent on where you are located — it is contingent on which infrastructure you build on. The sovereign stack works identically from Lagos, Accra, Nairobi, Karachi, Dhaka, Harare, or Manila. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 is deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours under your accounts, tested on mainnet before handoff. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete build for self-deployers. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Open a self-custody wallet — Trust Wallet or MetaMask — and back up the seed phrase before configuring anything else. Create your NOWPayments account and configure the self-custody wallet addresses as your payout destination. Open a Binance account and complete enough P2P setup to verify you can convert USDT to your local currency. Deploy your stack and configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint. Build your product pages with USD prices and confirm the checkout generates QR codes and live price feeds correctly. Run a mainnet test transaction from a second wallet to confirm the full pipeline. Do a test P2P conversion with a small amount of USDT to confirm the conversion process works end-to-end. Promote your store.
